text:
frank: Heads-up from the onboarding sprint: our TS quickstart 'bulk-migrate' demo is getting tons of 429s when customers stream historical embeddings.
lina: saw the trace. demo spawns a readable stream and pumps pages concurrently via the paginator, no client-side backpressure.
amir: can you paste the code?
frank: gist of it: ```ts
const stream = client.embeddings.streamPages(query)
stream.on('data', page => processPage(page))
// inside processPage we call client.embeddings.create for each item without concurrency guard
```
lina: that's the problem. streaming + unbounded per-page work == instant quota bursts. Also noticed the SDK retry strategy does immediate retries for 401/429, so we get retry storms.
amir: SDK parity note: Python has a StreamRateController utility that cooperatively yields when the bucket is empty. TS SDK doesn't expose a similar primitive.
frank: users told support the API is "rate limiting us out" which is misleading. it's sample behavior. we need either (A) export a stream-aware limiter from TS SDK or (B) change the demo to respect backpressure using async iterators + concurrency limiter.
lina: quick patch idea (low-risk): demo should use `for await (const page of client.embeddings.paginate(q))` plus small semaphore: ```ts
const sem = pLimit(4)
for await (const page of client.embeddings.paginate(q)) {
  await sem(() => processPage(page))
}
```
amir: agree. longer-term: export `createStreamThrottler({permitsPerSec, maxBurst})` and a small `paginator(concurrency)` option so streams signal when they want more. that solves ergonomics.
support-bot: adding KB note: "Bulk-migrate demo: if you see 429s, reduce per-page concurrency or use the SDK stream-throttler". link internal KB: https://kb.redwood-inference.dev/streaming-429s
frank: another UX bug: demo doesn't use AbortController to cancel inflight page work when the stream errors; we keep retrying and hit quota. we should wire cancellation through `signal` and ensure retries respect signal.
lina: good catch. put in small example in quickstart: `client.embeddings.create({ ..., signal })` and make retries abort when signal.aborted.
amir: auth race here too: when refresh happens while a long stream is in flight, we saw a burst of 401->retry loops. propose singleflight token refresh (mutex) + attach `x-client-stream-id` header so support can correlate long-running streams.
frank: what about exposing a diagnostics meter in the SDK dev build: `client.__dev.meter()` that reports current permits used, queue length, and avg latency. then demos can log and tune.
amir: dev-only meter makes sense; export behind `NODE_ENV !== 'production'` guard. helps customers tune before moving to prod.
support-bot: opened support queue item referencing this thread; we'll point customers to the demo update and KB.
deploy-bot: preview with demo change (p-limit + AbortController) deployed: https://deployments.redwood-inference.dev/pr/812
frank: action items: (1) patch demo to async-iterator + p-limit + AbortController (frank), (2) add KB & quickstart note (support), (3) plan SDK stream-throttler + singleflight refresh + dev meter in next sprint (amir/lina).
lina: timeline: demo patch + KB -> today. SDK primitives -> next sprint.
amir: will open RFC for stream-throttler API shape this week.
frank: thanks team 44d this should make long-running migrations much less painful for users.
